Hospital and diagnostics stocks to track. FY26 consolidated revenue growth and bed counts.

Hospitals

Apollo Hospitals - largest chain (revenue +16%, 10,900+ network beds)
Max Healthcare - high-quality North India (revenue +19%, ~4,966 beds)
Fortis Healthcare - pan-India hospitals and diagnostics (revenue +17%, ~4,500 beds)
Global Health, Medanta - quaternary care, North and East (revenue +19%, ~3,435 beds)
Narayana Hrudayalaya - cardiac and multispecialty (revenue +44%, ~5,800 beds; note the 44% is acquisition-led, India grew ~10%)
Aster DM Healthcare - South India focused post Middle East exit (revenue +14% proforma, merger with Quality Care underway)
KIMS - tertiary care leader in Telangana and AP (revenue +28%, expanding fast)
Rainbow Children's Medicare - only listed paediatric and maternity chain (revenue +12%, ~2,300 beds)
Yatharth Hospital - North India, fast bed expansion (Q3 revenue +46%, ~2,300 beds)
Park Medi World - recent listing, multispecialty

Diagnostics

Dr Lal PathLabs - diagnostics leader, North India (revenue +12%, 312 labs)
Metropolis Healthcare - pan-India labs (revenue ~+24%)
Thyrocare - pathology and preventive (revenue Rs 846 cr, ~32% over two years)
Vijaya Diagnostic - South India strong (revenue ~Rs 831 cr)
Krishna Diagnostics - pan-India, PPP model

Research them all.

Drivers: India's low hospital-bed penetration, expansion into Tier 2 and 3 cities, rising insurance coverage, and medical tourism. The key nuance across hospitals: most are in heavy bed-expansion mode, which lifts revenue but dents near-term margins and occupancy as new beds fill. KIMS, Rainbow and Yatharth all show this pattern. Judge them on a 2 to 3 year view.

Not SEBI registered. Not investment advice. Do your own research.
